clue.text: Without the Latest Trick disc, back to Brothers in Arms' pieces?

indicators.note: the latest letter of a word is its final one, so the clue word Trick loses its end

parts.note: the word as written, before its last letter goes
an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so only the end of Brothers is used

explanation.surface: A Dire Straits fan, short of one song (The Latest Trick), goes back to the Brothers in Arms album.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme is Dire Straits: The Latest Trick and Brothers in Arms are their song and album. 'Without the Latest' trims TRICK to TRIC; 'back to' takes the S ending Brothers.
explanation.definitionFit: The muscle at the back of the upper arm is one of the arm's component parts, so the playful question mark fits.

clue.text: Blowing horn, chime without me whistling sounds

indicators.note: blowing scatters things about, so the letters are rearranged
chime goes without the word me, leaving its first three letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician blowing a horn while a chime sounds, with whistling noises in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes ME from CHIME, leaving CHI; 'Blowing' then rearranges HORN with CHI.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical term for the wheezing or whistling noises heard in the chest through a stethoscope.

clue.text: Inched up piece of kit (percussion)

indicators.note: in a down light, up means the letters read from bottom to top
a piece of the phrase is a run of its letters, spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A drummer inched a piece of the percussion kit into position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece of' points to letters inside 'kit percussion', TPERC; 'up' turns them round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To move by inches is to go slowly and stealthily, past tense of creep.

clue.text: One setting up place for orchestra and singer

parts.note: the orchestra pit sits below the stage
Cher is the American pop singer

explanation.surface: Someone arranging a venue for an orchestra and a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One setting up' is someone who pitches a tent or a stall.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pitches a tent or a stall is putting it up, so a pitcher is one erecting things.

clue.text: Girl is in that place: America

parts.note: there means at that place
is shortens to 's

explanation.surface: A girl is over there, in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: House plant in a good way

parts.note: a lily is a flowering plant

explanation.surface: A house plant doing well.
explanation.definitionFit: To act in a saintly, pious manner is to behave righteously.

clue.text: Got better sax part; make new version in the middle?

indicators.note: the second piece goes in the middle of the first

parts.note: a saxophone's mouthpiece holds a reed
to cover a song is to record a new version of it

explanation.surface: A sax part improved after a new version was made, with something added mid-song.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover from illness is to recuperate, so the past tense means improved in health.

clue.text: Admit with promise of endless jazz to captivate listener

indicators.note: to captivate is to hold within, so the second piece goes inside
the last letter is cut off the word for jazz

parts.note: swing is a jazz style
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: A promise of non-stop jazz is used to win over a listener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admit' here means formally admitting someone to office, and 'with promise' is the oath they take; 'endless' and 'to captivate' are the two signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Officials are admitted to office by taking an oath, the promise in the definition.

clue.text: Sex sessions for TVs?

parts.note: gender is another word for sex
a bender is a drinking session

explanation.surface: Racy sessions made for television.
explanation.walkthrough: TV here is short for transvestite, not television.
explanation.definitionFit: TV abbreviates transvestite, someone who blurs or crosses the usual dress codes of men and women.

clue.text: Tunnel of Love run through live

indicators.note: the pieces run through the middle of the other word

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Tunnel of Love, a Dire Straits song, run through live.
explanation.walkthrough: Tunnel of Love is a Dire Straits song; 'Tunnel' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To bore is to drill or dig, so it can mean to tunnel.

clue.text: Music character around clubs left rebel in Dire Straits

indicators.note: something in dire straits is in a mess, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: C is the card abbreviation for clubs
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musical figure goes round, the clubs left by a rebel in the band Dire Straits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is a link here; the band name doubles as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The G clef at the start of a high-voice stave is a symbol used in written music.

clue.text: Put an end to drink

definitions.meaning: to ... a rumour is to stop it

explanation.surface: Stop drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch is to stamp out, and the word is also a whisky distilled in Scotland.

clue.text: Articulation of Labour's goal

definitions.meaning: labour in childbirth ends with the baby being born

explanation.surface: How the Labour Party expresses its aims.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour looks political; it is childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: A speaker's elocution is their style of speech, and the birth of a baby is what labour leads to.

clue.text: Playing lead off Day Tripper, it's so far away in song

definitions.text: it's so far away in song

indicators.note: playing with the letters rearranges them
the lead letter of the word Day comes off

explanation.surface: Playing Day Tripper, the Beatles song, but cutting out the lead part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead off' removes D from Day, and 'Playing' shuffles AY with TRIPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: The First World War song says it's a long way to this Irish town.

clue.text: No damage — it's absurd

definitions.meaning: damage is slang for cost, so having no cost at all

explanation.surface: A claim of no damage is ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damage' is slang for the cost of something, as in what's the damage?
explanation.definitionFit: Something without a cost is literally free of charge, and the word also means hilariously funny.

clue.text: Mark Knopfler's final piece in group

indicators.note: the letter sits inside the word for group

parts.note: a band is a musical group

indicators.note: the final piece of the word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Mark Knopfler's last track with Dire Straits.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark Knopfler is the Dire Straits frontman; his first name is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand is an identifying mark, like the stamp burned onto cattle.

clue.text: Echo in Romeo and Juliet — concert lacks initial tweak

indicators.note: Echo sits between the two letters

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet
Juliet is J in the NATO alphabet
Echo is E in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: the concert word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a gig is a concert

explanation.surface: A Romeo and Juliet production echoes; a concert misses its opening tweak.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejig something is to adjust or rearrange it slightly.

clue.text: State cost to record company

parts.note: EMI is a British record label
a rate is a charge or cost

explanation.surface: Telling a record company the cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb; it is a country.
explanation.definitionFit: A country ruled by an emir, such as those in the Gulf, is a kind of state.

clue.text: Those in studio on about arrangements

parts.note: re means on the subject of
C is short for circa, about
orders are arrangements, as in the order of things

explanation.surface: People in a studio discussing arrangements.
explanation.definitionFit: Recording machines, or the people making records, are found in a recording studio.

clue.text: Makes up for bad songs in shows

parts.note: food gone off is bad
a band's set is the songs it plays in a show

explanation.surface: Good gigs make up for poor songs.
explanation.definitionFit: To offset is to counterbalance, compensating for something.

clue.text: Rapidly gets Playboy with guilt?

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute playboy
sin is wrongdoing that brings guilt

explanation.surface: A playboy feeling guilty earns fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To rake in money is to earn it quickly and in large amounts.

clue.text: Stay until end of international tour, almost set in stone

indicators.note: the pieces are set inside the word for stone

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

indicators.note: the word for tour is cut before its final letter

explanation.surface: Staying to the end of an international tour, almost set in stone.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds; 'almost' trims the tour word and 'set in' places the pieces inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit out a performance is to remain seated through it to the finish.

clue.text: Winged one short piece during Telegraph Road

parts.note: a wire is a telegram

indicators.note: the word for piece is cut short by one letter

parts.note: a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: A brief part of the Dire Straits song Telegraph Road.
explanation.walkthrough: Telegraph Road is a Dire Straits song, split here into its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A plover found on St Helena is a bird, and anything with wings is a flying creature.

clue.text: Strong instrumental passages (Making Movies)

parts.note: F is forte, loud or strong in music
licks are short guitar phrases

explanation.surface: Strong guitar passages on Making Movies, the Dire Straits album.
explanation.definitionFit: Flicks is informal slang for films or the cinema.

clue.text: Lines from one topless deer, we hear

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the first letter is taken off the top of the deer, in this down light

parts.note: Bambi is the famous Disney deer

explanation.surface: Lines spoken by a topless deer, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' marks Bambi as a deer known by name; there is no sound device.
explanation.definitionFit: These are metrical feet of an unstressed then stressed syllable, the building blocks of verse lines.

clue.text: Track from programme following career

indicators.note: the programme piece comes after

parts.note: to career is to race along
a course is a programme of study

explanation.surface: A track from an album that follows an artist's career.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses run on this racing circuit, a kind of track.

clue.text: Has to put out Money for Nothing

indicators.note: one letter stands in for another

parts.note: to oust is to put out or expel
nothing looks like O, zero

explanation.surface: Someone must put out the Dire Straits single Money for Nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Money for Nothing', the Dire Straits song, means M replaces O.
explanation.definitionFit: Being obliged to do something is the same as being required to do it.

clue.text: Mass, according to volume, has God welcoming opposing points

indicators.note: the god word takes the points into its middle

parts.note: a deity is a god
N and S are opposite compass points

explanation.surface: A sermon on how God welcomes conflicting viewpoints, loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics this is mass per unit volume.

clue.text: Gives clue to fill bottom

indicators.note: the clue word fills the inside of the bottom word

parts.note: ass is American slang for the backside
a sign is a clue or hint

explanation.surface: Handing over a hint to plug a gap at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot or allocate something to someone is to hand it over.
